architecture_summary.operational_context: cloud-hosted web application with containerized services deployed in a VPC; Nginx terminates TLS at edge, FlaskAPI runs in private subnet, PostgreSQL in isolated data subnet with no direct internet access

threat_actors.name: External Opportunistic Attacker
threat_actors.motivation: financial gain, credential harvesting, service disruption, cryptomining
non_capabilities: no insider knowledge of internal network topology
no ability to bypass WAF rules without detection

threat_actors.name: Malicious Insider (Developer/Operator)
threat_actors.motivation: data theft, sabotage, espionage, intellectual property exfiltration
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: legitimate internal network access via corporate VPN and CI/CD pipeline access
non_capabilities: no direct access to production database without approval workflow and audit logging
no ability to modify infrastructure-as-code without mandatory peer review
no physical access to hardware security modules or key management systems
no root access to production Kubernetes nodes without break-glass procedure

attack_paths.entry_point: HTTPS port 443 on Nginx reverse proxy
attack_paths.impact: Initial foothold in DMZ; potential lateral movement to application layer via compromised proxy
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Nginx is internet-exposed; vulnerabilities in Nginx (CVE-2021-23017, CVE-2022-41741) or misconfigurations (path traversal, header smuggling) are actively exploited in the wild

attack_paths.entry_point: HTTP API endpoints exposed via Nginx (e.g., /api/v1/users, /api/v1/upload)
attack_paths.impact: Direct application compromise; SQL injection or command injection leading to data exfiltration or remote code execution
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Flask APIs frequently contain injection flaws (SQLi via raw queries, command injection via subprocess, path traversal); OWASP Top 10 risks map directly to this entry point

attack_paths.entry_point: Internal HTTP API calls from Nginx to FlaskAPI (port 8000/5000)
attack_paths.impact: Compromise of application server after initial Nginx breach; access to business logic, session tokens, and database credentials
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: If Nginx compromised (AP-001), attacker can send malicious requests to FlaskAPI; trust between layers often overly permissive with no mutual TLS or request validation

attack_paths.entry_point: Database connection from FlaskAPI to PostgreSQL (port 5432)
attack_paths.impact: Persistent access to database; data exfiltration at rest, credential theft, backdoor user creation
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Database credentials often stored in config files or environment variables on FlaskAPI; compromised app server yields direct DB access; PostgreSQL superuser or CREATEROLE privileges enable persistence

attack_paths.entry_point: Internal network segment (VPC subnet) carrying traffic between Nginx-FlaskAPI and FlaskAPI-PostgreSQL
attack_paths.impact: Interception of sensitive data in transit: API tokens, PII, database credentials, session cookies
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires network-level access (compromised host in same VPC, malicious insider, or cloud provider insider); TLS between layers mitigates but internal segments may lack encryption (mTLS not enforced)

mitigations.control_name: Application Software Security - Secure Coding Practices
Automated Vulnerability Scanning and Patch Management
Identity and Access Management - Least Privilege Database Roles

findings.severity_rationale: Internet-exposed Nginx with known vulnerability history provides initial access vector; successful exploit leads to DMZ foothold and lateral movement opportunity
FlaskAPI directly accessible via public endpoints with high likelihood of injection flaws; compromise yields direct data access and RCE potential
Lateral movement from compromised Nginx to FlaskAPI feasible due to excessive trust between tiers; network segmentation partially mitigates but application-layer validation missing
Database credentials on FlaskAPI host enable direct PostgreSQL access; excessive privileges (superuser/CREATEROLE) allow persistence and data exfiltration at rest
Internal network traffic unencrypted (no mTLS) allows credential and data interception if attacker gains VPC-level access; low likelihood but high impact if realized
